actions.name: get_form_responses
actions.description: Retrieve responses. Returns form responses and date and time of form landing and submission. Very recent responses (say within the last 30 minutes) may not be returned. Considering using Typeform webhooks instead for real-time submission data.

page_size.description: If your typeform has more than 1000 responses, use the since/until or before/after query parameters to narrow the scope of your request.

since.description: Limit request to responses submitted since the specified date and time, inclusive. Could be passed as int (timestamp in seconds) or in ISO 8601 format, UTC time, to the second, with T as a delimiter between the date and time (2020-03-20T14:00:59).

until.description: Limit request to responses submitted until the specified date and time, inclusive. Could be passed as int (timestamp in seconds) or in ISO 8601 format, UTC time, to the second, with T as a delimiter between the date and time (2020-03-20T14:00:59).

after.description: Return responses submitted after this cursor (exclusive).

before.description: Return responses submitted before this cursor (exclusive).

included_response_ids.description: Limit request to the specified response_id values. Use a comma-separated list to specify more than one response_id value.

excluded_response_ids.description: Comma-separated list of response_ids to be excluded from the response.

response_type.description: Limit responses to only those which are of the provided response type. It is expected to be passed as a comma separated list of values, e.g. response_type=partial,completed. This parameter changes since/until filter, so if completed responses are requested it will filter by submitted_at, if partial responses are requested it will filter by staged_at, otherwise - landed_at. Default value is completed.

completed.description: This query param is deprecated, please use response_type param instead. Limit responses to only those which were started (completed=false), but not completed (completed=true) (the respondent did not submit their answers). When completed=false, the responses do not have answers, hidden or calculate members. This parameter changes since/until filter, so if completed=true, it will filter by submitted_at, otherwise - landed_at. Default value is completed=true.

sort.description: How to sort the returned responses. Default is submitted_at,desc for completed responses, staged_at,desc for partial responses, and landed_at,desc for started responses.

query.description: Search for an exact phrase within answer values, hidden field values, and variable values. A response matches when any of the three contains the phrase as a contiguous sequence of words.

fields.description: Show only specified fields in answers section. If response does not have answers for specified fields, there will be null. Use a comma-separated list to specify more than one field value.

answered_fields.description: Limit request to only responses that include the specified fields in answers section. Use a comma-separated list to specify more than one field value - response will contain at least one of the specified fields.

form_id.description: The form's id, as in its link (https://mysite.typeform.com/to/u6nXL7 → u6nXL7); list_forms lists them

actions.name: search_responses
actions.description: Search responses using advanced filters. Retrieves form responses using a structured filter format that supports combining multiple conditions on answers, metadata, tags, hidden fields, response IDs, and submission time. Prefer this endpoint over `GET /forms/{form_id}/responses` when you need to filter by answer values or combine conditions.

form_id.description: The form's id, as in its link (https://mysite.typeform.com/to/u6nXL7 → u6nXL7); list_forms lists them

after_response_id.description: A response ID used as a pagination cursor. Traverses the complete set of responses in the order the system processed them (`submitted_at`), without repeats. Cannot be combined with sort clauses.

answered_fields.description: A list of form field IDs.

before_response_id.description: A response ID used as a pagination cursor. Traverses the complete set of responses in the order the system processed them (`submitted_at`), without repeats. Cannot be combined with sort clauses.

fields.description: A list of form field IDs.

filter_group.description: A set of filters combined with a logical AND. A response is included only when every filter matches.

field.description:
The field to filter on. Supported values:
  - `response_id` — filter by response IDs
  - `timestamp` — filter by submission time (use with `interval`)
  - `tags` — filter by response tags
  - `answers.{field_id}` — filter by the answer to a specific form field
  - `metadata.{key}` — filter by a metadata attribute (e.g. `metadata.platform`)
  - `hidden.{key}` — filter by a hidden field value

operator.description:
How `value` is compared to the field:
  - `equals` — exact match against `value.text`, `value.number`, or `value.boolean`
  - `any_of` — matches any entry in `value.text_list`
  - `interval` — matches values inside `value.interval` (used with `timestamp`)

value.description: Filter operand. Provide exactly one field, matching the `operator` (`equals` uses `text`/`number`/`boolean`, `any_of` uses `text_list`, `interval` uses `interval`).

interval.description: A time range in Unix seconds. Both bounds are inclusive; either bound may be omitted for an open-ended range.

query.description: Search for an exact phrase within answer values, hidden field values, and variable values. A response matches when any of the three contains the phrase as a contiguous sequence of words.

response_type.description: Which response types to include. Defaults to `["completed"]` when omitted.

actions.name: get_audio_master_file
actions.description:
Get audio master file (download). Retrieves the processed master audio file URL. This endpoint should be polled to check the transcoding status.

**Download Process:**
1. After requesting the master file (POST), poll this endpoint to check the transcoding `status`
2. When `status` is `"ready"`, the `url` field contains the download URL for the processed audio
3. Use the returned URL to download the audio file

**Status Values:**
- `none`: Audio master is not yet requested
- `preparing`: Audio master is being prepared
- `ready`: Audio is ready for download (URL provided)

**Polling Recommendations:**
- Poll every 2-3 seconds initially
- After 30 seconds, increase polling interval to 5-10 s...

**Note:** This endpoint is idempotent - calling it multiple times for the same audio will not restart processing.
